item.title: Overview
item.description:
Using Meshery Designs to Manage Your Infrastructure

Meshery is a versatile platform designed to streamline the lifecycle, configuration, and performance management of infrastructure across Kubernetes clusters.

Designs in Meshery

Meshery employs the concept of Designs as a fundamental construct for managing infrastructure. Designs provide a structured way to organize and deploy various components of your infrastructure. To do so, Meshery utilizes a declarative approach to infrastructure management, similar to Kubernetes manifests. Meshery Designs are written in YAML and are validated against a schema.

item.title: Registering a Connection
item.description:
A Connection is how Meshery tracks and manages a resource - a Kubernetes cluster, a Grafana instance, a Prometheus server, and many more. The Connection Wizard is the guided, in-UI way to register a new Connection or reconfigure an existing one, without hand-editing YAML or memorizing API payloads.

item.title: Configuring Meshery Operator, MeshSync, and Broker
item.description:
Every Kubernetes cluster that Meshery manages is served by up to three components: Meshery Operator, MeshSync, and Meshery Broker. Their defaults work out of the box, but production clusters routinely need tuning: narrowing discovery scope, keeping Secret contents out of Meshery’s database, exposing the Broker across network boundaries, or skipping in-cluster components entirely.

This guide walks through the full configuration surface of all three components: what each setting does, how to change it, its default, and the behavioral impact of changing it. It is written for platform engineers operating real clusters with kubectl, mesheryctl, and the Meshery UI.

item.title: Bringing Existing Infrastructure Under Meshery Management
item.description: Most clusters do not arrive empty. They carry months or years of accumulated Deployments, CRDs, operators, and Secrets, deployed by pipelines that predate Meshery and that will keep running after it. This guide is for the platform engineer bringing that kind of estate - a brownfield - under Meshery’s management: what connecting a live cluster actually does, what it deliberately does not do, and what to evaluate before you connect.

item.title: Deploying a Design
item.description:
Use this guide to put a Design onto one or more of your Kubernetes clusters, check what happened, and remove it again. Meshery deploys a design to the clusters you pick from your Environments, so you can deploy the same design to a staging cluster and a production cluster in one pass.

Before you begin

  • A design in Meshery. Create one with the Design Configurator or import your Kubernetes manifests, Helm chart, Docker Compose file, or Kustomize package.
  • At least one Kubernetes Connection in the Connected state.
  • That Connection assigned to an Environment. The deployment wizard only offers clusters that belong to an Environment. To assign one, see Sharing a Cluster with Your Team, or use the Environments column in Lifecycle → Connections.
  • Permission to deploy designs. If the Deploy action is disabled, ask your organization admin.

Deploy a design

  1. Open Configuration → Designs.

item.title: Sharing a Cluster with Your Team
item.description:
A Kubernetes cluster you connect to Meshery is private to you until you share it. Use this guide to let your teammates see the cluster, deploy designs to it, and work with its resources, without handing out your kubeconfig. You share a cluster in three steps:

  1. Put the cluster’s Connection in an Environment.
  2. Attach the Environment to a Workspace.
  3. Assign your teammates’ teams to the Workspace.

Before you begin

  • A Meshery Server signed in with a Remote Provider, such as Meshery Cloud. Organizations, teams, and other users come from the Remote Provider. With the Local provider you are the only user, although you can still use Environments to group your own clusters.
  • The cluster registered as a Kubernetes Connection. See Registering a Connection.
  • Teammates who belong to a team in your organization. Your provider manages teams and invitations.
  • Permission to create Environments and Workspaces and to assign resources to them. If a button is disabled, ask your organization admin.

Create an Environment and add the cluster

  1. Open Lifecycle → Environments and click Create.
  2. Enter a name, such as staging, and an optional description, then save.
  3. On the new Environment’s card, click Assigned Connections. The <environment> Resources dialog opens.
  4. Move the cluster’s Connection from the available list to the assigned list, then click Save.

You can also assign Environments from Lifecycle → Connections: use the Environments column on the cluster’s row.

item.title: Kubernetes Connection Lifecycle
item.description:
This guide explains what actually happens when Meshery manages a Kubernetes Connection: the components Meshery deploys, how it stays in sync with your cluster, the connectivity it depends on, and the knobs and diagnostics you use to operate it. For the generic connection state machine that applies to every kind of connection, see Connections; for how to register one in the first place, see Registering a Connection.

What happens when you connect a cluster

item.title: Envoy WASM Filter Management
item.description:
Meshery offers powerful features that simplify the management of Envoy WASM filters in Istio.

Meshery UI and CLI Integration

  • Import WASM Envoy Filters: Easily import your WebAssembly Envoy filters into Meshery using the intuitive UI or the command-line interface (CLI).
  • Publish and Clone Filters: Share your filters with the community by publishing them in the Meshery Catalog and make it effortless for others to clone them.
  • Download WASM Binaries: Access and download WebAssembly binaries directly from your Remote Provider like Meshery Cloud.
  • Efficient Data Plane Design: Seamlessly design and deploy Istio and Envoy data planes using Meshery.
  • Contribute to Open Source: Get involved with the cloud native community by contributing to any of the open source wasm-filters developed by the Meshery community.

item.title: GitOps with Meshery
item.description:
Meshery Snapshot GitHub Action

  • See your deployment before you merge
  • Connect Meshery to your GitHub repo and see changes pull request-to-pull request
  • Get snapshots of your infrastructure directly in your PRs

Using Meshery's SnapShot GitHub Action

See your deployment before you merge. Connect Meshery to your GitHub repo and see changes pull request-to-pull request. Get snapshots of your infrastructure directly in your PRs.

See Extension: Meshery Snapshot for more details.

item.title: Managing Connections
item.description:
Meshery manages hundreds of different types of cloud native infrastructure. See the full set of integrations.

Cloud Native Infrastructure Lifecycle Management

Meshery Adapters can optionally be deployed to provide deep support of different types of infrastructure, so that you can learn and compare different infrastructure functionality. Once you have selected to operate a given infrastructure, Meshery will assist you with ongoing operations.

Meshery automates the provisioning of various infrastructurees, allowing users to select different configuration profiles in order to support a variety of deployment models.

item.title: Managing Events with Notification Center
item.description:
Meshery continuously tracks activities affecting your infrastructure and workloads. Meshery generates a variety of events, reflecting activities affecting the design and operation of your infrastructure whether those activities are directly or indirectly performed through Meshery operations.

What is the Notification Center?

The Notification Center is a dedicated panel in Meshery’s UI that helps you monitor, understand, and respond to events across your system. It acts as a central place where you can see important updates related to your infrastructure, workloads, and Meshery’s internal operations.
